reading.body:
Tecnodati S.R.L. is an unverified OpenStreetMap point in Italy, tagged as a data center, with no operator, no website, and no confirmed capacity.

The record carries a name that fits its tag. "Dati" is Italian for data, and the S.R.L. suffix is the ordinary Italian limited-liability form, so the entry reads as a plausible small IT or data-services business rather than a mis-tagged one. The same dataset contains Italian records whose names plainly belong to other industries, an accounting firm, a foam manufacturer, an auto-club branch, which makes this one comparatively credible on naming alone.

Credibility of a name is not evidence of a facility. The record has no operator, no website, and no megawatt figure, and the research note states that confirmation against a business registration or operator site was not completed. Nothing here establishes that compute is running at these coordinates, let alone how much.

For a question about compute and the grid, this entry contributes a location and nothing else. It sits near Parma, about 18.6 miles from Parma Airport, at coordinates in northern Italy. It cannot be counted toward regional data-center capacity, and it should not be read as evidence that Italy's grid or power supply is under pressure from AI workloads. It is a candidate for verification, not a data point about scale.
